scenes.title: Italy
scenes.subtitle: A history told only by its sources

scenes.caption: Photo 1875
scenes.text: Rome was founded as a kingdom in 753 BC and became a republic in 509 BC.

scenes.caption: Photo 1880
scenes.text: In the 19th century, Italian unification led to the establishment of an Italian nation-state under the House of Savoy.

scenes.caption: Photo 1880
scenes.text: The partial infringement of the Treaty of London (1915) led to the sentiment of a mutilated victory among radical nationalists, contributing to the rise of the fascist dictatorship of Benito Mussolini in 1922.

scenes.caption: Photo 1893 · Rome
scenes.text: It is generally believed that around 2000 BC, the Ligures occupied a large area of the peninsula, including much of north-western Italy and all of northern Tuscany.

scenes.caption: Photo 1880 · Rome
scenes.text: According to the founding myth of Rome, the city was founded on 21 April 753 BC by twin brothers Romulus and Remus, who descended from the Trojan prince Aeneas and who were grandsons of Numitor of Alba Longa.

scenes.caption: Photo 1893 · Rome
scenes.text: Here their interests collided with those of the Greeks, especially in the 6th century BC, when Phoceans of Italy founded colonies along the coast of France, Catalonia and Corsica.

scenes.caption: Photo 1875 · Rome
scenes.text: In 751, the Lombards seized Ravenna, ending Byzantine rule in northern Italy.

scenes.caption: Photo 1880 · Rome
scenes.text: In 756 Frankish forces defeated the Lombards and gave the Papacy legal authority over much of central Italy, establishing the Papal States.

scenes.caption: Photo 1875 · Rome
scenes.text: In 800, Charlemagne was crowned emperor of what would become the Holy Roman Empire.

scenes.caption: Photo 1890 · Rome
scenes.text: Venice was the first real international financial center, which slowly emerged from the 9th century to its peak in the 14th century.

scenes.caption: Photo 1880 · Rome
scenes.text: Since the 13th century, as armies became primarily composed of mercenaries, prosperous city-states could field considerable forces despite their low populations.

scenes.caption: Photo 1890 · Rome
scenes.text: Over the 15th century, the most powerful city-states annexed their smaller neighbours: Florence took Pisa in 1406, Venice captured Padua and Verona, while the Duchy of Milan annexed nearby areas including Pavia and Parma.

scenes.caption: Photo 1893 · Rome
scenes.text: From the Peace of Cateau-Cambrésis to the War of the Spanish Succession, the Spanish Habsburgs ruled Sicily, Naples, and Milan; these territories passed to the Austrian Habsburgs in 1700.

scenes.caption: Photo 1880 · Rome
scenes.text: The War of the Spanish Succession (1701–1714) was triggered by the death without issue of the last Habsburg king of Spain, Charles II, who fixed the Spanish inheritance on Philip, Duke of Anjou, the grandson of King Louis XIV of…

scenes.caption: Photo 1893 · Rome
scenes.text: Corsica passed from the Republic of Genoa to France in 1769 after the Treaty of Versailles.

scenes.caption: Photo 1852
scenes.text: It is difficult to pin down exact dates for the beginning and end of Italian reunification, but most scholars agree that it began with the end of Napoleonic rule and the Congress of Vienna in 1815, and approximately ended with…

scenes.caption: Photo 1860
scenes.text: In 1820, Spaniards successfully revolted over disputes about their Constitution, which influenced the development of a similar movement in Italy.

scenes.caption: Photo 1860
scenes.text: The leader of the 1821 revolutionary movement in Piedmont was Santorre di Santarosa, who wanted to remove the Austrians and unify Italy under the House of Savoy.

scenes.caption: Photo 1900
scenes.text: Starting from the late 19th century, Italy developed its own colonial Empire.

scenes.caption: Photo 1900
scenes.text: The nascent Kingdom of Italy invaded and occupied Romagna (the eastern portion of the Papal States) in 1860, leaving only Latium in the pope's domains.

scenes.caption: Photo 1893
scenes.text: The subsequent Treaty of Rome (1924) led to the annexation of the city of Fiume to Italy.

scenes.title: What the sources leave out
scenes.text: Between 1559 and 1700, the sources consulted give no precise date.
